to exercise the pipeline, and every one carries validated_by_human=false.

Before this index backs any real assessment: open the primary source, confirm
the section number and the obligation, replace `requirement` with accurate

standards whose requirement text may not be reproduced in a circulating index,
so they are excluded. Testing coverage moved to NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1, which
is free and covers the same obligation.

requirements.requirement: Identify critical business functions and determine the impact of disruption on those functions.
Establish recovery time objectives and recovery point objectives for each critical business function and supporting system.
Address a range of disruption scenarios including natural disaster, facility loss, and technology failure.
Include destructive cyber events, including ransomware, among the disruption scenarios planned for and tested.
Document recovery expectations for critical third-party service providers, including agreed recovery objectives and evidence they can be met.
Maintain documented recovery procedures for each planned scenario, sufficient for the responsible party to execute them.
Maintain current emergency contact information, including an escalation path with primary and backup contacts for critical roles.

Create and maintain a written business continuity plan identifying procedures reasonably designed to enable the firm to meet its obligations to customers and counterparties during a significant business disruption.
Review the business continuity plan at least annually and update it to reflect material changes to operations, structure, business, or location.
Maintain and update emergency contact information provided to FINRA.
Address business continuity and contingency planning for services provided by third parties, including the institution's own contingency for a provider failure.
Document activation criteria and the authority to activate the plan, so it is unambiguous when the plan takes effect and who declares it.
Test the contingency plan to validate that recovery procedures are effective, and document the results of each test including lessons identified.
